args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx
Classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This report compares the creditors' committee's redlined Plan of Reorganization (the "Committee Markup") against the debtor's original Plan of Reorganization (the "Debtor Plan"), reconciling each deviation against (i) the base deal materials, (ii) the valuation summary and disclosure-statement excerpts reflected in the schedules and exhibits, and (iii) the controlling partner instruction in the deal-team correspondence.

The Committee Markup accepts most firm-standard and Debtor Plan provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  1. Silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping basket;
  2. Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition to add carve-outs for regulatory action of the type presently at issue; and
  3. A new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations.

Cross-reference to the disclosure schedules and Exhibit B demonstrates that each of these markup changes interacts with, and in two cases is contradicted by, scheduled exceptions and the agreed survival matrix. Under the controlling deal-team instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs remain open negotiating points and should be rejected or tightly cabined.

Recommendation at a glance:

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT / CONCEDE (per controlling client instruction).
  • Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT; restore Debtor Plan cap; require express redline and disclosure of quantum.
  • MAE regulatory-action carve-outs: REJECT or narrow; Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries make the carve-out outcome-determinative.
  • Shortened survival / limitation period for core reps: REJECT — WALK-AWAY issue; Exhibit B survival matrix controls.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
II. SOURCE MATERIALS REVIEWED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

A. Debtor Plan / Base Materials
   Matter file describing the operative Plan of Reorganization framework, including representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to confirmation/closing analogues, indemnification, termination, and related plan-support mechanics. These materials are the baseline against which the Committee Markup is measured.

B. Committee Markup (Counterparty Redline)
   Redline accepting most firm-standard provisions while introducing the three deviations catalogued in Section III.

C. Valuation Summary, Transmittal Context, and Disclosure-Statement Excerpts
   Reflected in the schedules and exhibits package:
   • Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup's MAE carve-outs;
   • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently reallocate;
   • Exhibit B — survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts.
   Per the schedules package, scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base bankruptcy-restructuring materials.

D. Deal-Team Correspondence (Controlling Instruction)
   Partner email thread. The latest message revises analysis priorities: the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded; only the latest message controls. This report follows the controlling instruction.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Debtor Plan Position (Baseline)
   The Debtor Plan maintains a stated indemnification cap at the negotiated quantum and employs a traditional deductible basket: the indemnifying party is responsible only for losses exceeding the basket threshold, and losses within the basket do not count toward recovery once the threshold is crossed. Cap and basket operate together with the retained-liability construct on Schedule 5.2 so that known retained items are ring-fenced and do not erode the general indemnity stack.

B. Committee Markup Position
   (i) Cap: The indemnification cap is silently reduced — the redline does not call out the quantum change in a manner that would be apparent on a provision-level skim; the reduced figure appears only in the operative numeric reference.
   (ii) Basket: The basket is converted from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar) basket — once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnified party recovers from dollar one.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Valuation / Disclosure Excerpts
   Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. Under the Debtor Plan architecture, Schedule 5.2 retained items sit outside (or are expressly carved from) the general indemnity and therefore do not consume the cap. A silent cap reduction, paired with a tipping basket, has two compounding effects against the valuation and disclosure posture:
   • Known Schedule 5.2 items, if not cleanly excluded from the redefined indemnity, can tip the basket and then draw against a smaller cap, transferring economic exposure from the committee/creditor constituency back onto the reorganized debtor or the estate residual in a manner not reflected in the valuation summary or disclosure-statement recovery analysis.
   • Because the cap reduction is silent, the disclosure-statement description of indemnity economics and the valuation summary's treatment of contingent indemnity drag are no longer accurate unless both are expressly updated.
   Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials; accordingly, Schedule 5.2's retained-liability list must be re-mapped line-by-line to the revised cap and tipping-basket mechanics before any acceptance.

D. Client Instruction / Priority
   Controlling correspondence: client will concede the basket conversion. The cap reduction is not covered by that concession and remains contested.

E. Disposition and Recommended Counter
   1. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE, consistent with controlling client instruction. Document the concession expressly in the next turn so the record is clear that only the basket structure — not the cap — is yielded.
   2. Cap reduction: REJECT. Require restoration of the Debtor Plan cap quantum. Insist that any future proposed change to the cap appear as an express, conspicuous redline with a blackline comparison of the numeric cap and an updated Schedule 5.2 mapping.
   3. Condition any basket concession on: (a) express exclusion of all Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities from basket-tipping and from cap burn; (b) conforming edits to the disclosure-statement indemnity summary and valuation sensitivity; and (c) no reciprocal silent changes elsewhere in Article on indemnification / plan settlements.

F. Risk if Accepted As-Is
   Silent cap reduction plus tipping basket plus unmapped Schedule 5.2 items produces an unquantified transfer of downside to the estate/reorganized debtor, undermines disclosure adequacy, and creates confirmation risk on feasibility and fairness grounds to the extent recoveries assumed in the valuation summary no longer hold.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect Definition; Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Debtor Plan Position (Baseline)
   The Debtor Plan MAE definition follows a conventional formulation: MAE means a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, condition (financial or otherwise), or results of operations of the debtor (taken as a whole), subject only to standard market carve-outs (general economic/industry conditions, market movements, acts of war/terrorism, changes in law of general applicability, etc.) that themselves contain customary "disproportionate effect" push-backs. Regulatory actions specific to the debtor or of the type actually pending are not carved out of MAE.

B. Committee Markup Position
   The MAE definition is revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. As drafted, the carve-out would exclude from MAE the consequences of the pending regulatory matters, thereby preventing those matters (and their reasonably foreseeable outgrowths) from supporting an MAE-based condition failure, termination right, or related plan-support remedy.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Valuation / Disclosure Excerpts
   Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. Because scheduled exceptions control over general base-material statements:
   • The two Schedule 3.7 inquiries are precisely the fact pattern the new carve-out is designed to neutralize.
   • If the carve-out is accepted, adverse developments in either inquiry — including enforcement actions, fines, operational restrictions, or license consequences — would be unavailable to establish MAE, even if they would otherwise meet the materiality threshold under the Debtor Plan definition.
   • The valuation summary and disclosure-statement risk factors that treat regulatory outcomes as potentially value-affecting would be misaligned with plan conditions and termination/MAE mechanics, creating a disclosure and feasibility gap: the plan would describe regulatory risk as material while simultaneously contracting it out of the MAE trigger.

D. Client Instruction / Priority
   Controlling correspondence does not authorize concession on MAE. MAE regulatory carve-outs remain a live issue to be defended.

E. Disposition and Recommended Counter
   1. REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs as proposed.
   2. Primary counter: restore Debtor Plan MAE definition with no regulatory-action carve-out keyed to the Schedule 3.7 subject matter.
   3. Fallback (only if commercial pressure requires a limited move): permit a narrow carve-out limited to (a) the specific existence of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries as disclosed, and (b) the ordinary-course continuation of those inquiries without more — expressly preserving MAE treatment for any material adverse development, expansion of scope, enforcement action, penalty, operational restriction, or resolution on terms materially adverse to the debtor or reorganized debtor. Include a disproportionate-impact push-back if any general "changes in regulation" language is retained.
   4. Require conforming disclosure-statement and valuation updates so that MAE mechanics, Schedule 3.7, and risk-factor language remain consistent.

F. Risk if Accepted As-Is
   Acceptance would nullify MAE protection for the central known regulatory risk on the file, shift that risk entirely onto plan constituencies relying on MAE-triggered rights, and create confirmation/disclosure vulnerability given Schedule 3.7's prominence in the disclosure package.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 3 — Shortened Survival / New Limitation Period for Core Representations
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Debtor Plan Position (Baseline)
   Survival of representations is governed by the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B. Core representations (including those tied to authority, capitalization/structure analogues appropriate to a plan context, financial statements, absence of undisclosed liabilities as qualified by schedules, and regulatory status) survive for the periods specified in Exhibit B — which are longer than the markup's proposed limitation period.

B. Committee Markup Position
   A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, truncating the window in which breaches may be asserted relative to the Exhibit B matrix.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Valuation / Disclosure Excerpts
   Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts. Under the schedules package rule that scheduled exceptions and exhibits control over general base statements:
   • Exhibit B is the operative survival schedule; a conflicting general limitation period in the markup cannot silently override it.
   • Shortened survival interacts adversely with Schedule 3.7 (regulatory inquiries often mature on timelines longer than a truncated survival window) and Schedule 5.2 (retained-liability true-ups and indemnity claims frequently surface after consummation on the longer Exhibit B cadence).
   • The valuation summary's treatment of contingent claim tails and the disclosure-statement description of post-effective-date remedies presuppose the Exhibit B periods. A shortened limitation period without conforming Exhibit B and disclosure edits would misstate creditor and estate protections.

D. Client Instruction / Priority
   Controlling correspondence: any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier thread messages that suggested flexibility on survival are superseded and must not be followed.

E. Disposition and Recommended Counter
   1. REJECT in full. Treat as non-negotiable per controlling client instruction.
   2. Require express reaffirmation that Exhibit B remains the sole survival matrix for core representations, with no general limitation period cutting back Exhibit B.
   3. If the committee seeks clarity rather than shortening, offer a conforming cross-reference: "Survival of representations shall be exclusively as set forth in Exhibit B," and delete the markup's freestanding shortened limitation period.
   4. Do not trade survival for concessions on other deviations; walk-away status means the point is not available as currency.

F. Risk if Accepted As-Is
   Acceptance would breach the client's walk-away directive, contradict Exhibit B, impair post-effective-date remedies tied to core reps (including those implicated by Schedule 3.7 regulatory matters and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities), and misalign the disclosure-statement remedy narrative with the operative plan.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION MATRIX
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Deviation                         | Baseline (Debtor Plan / Exhibits)      | Markup Change                         | Controlling Schedule/Exhibit        | Client Posture (Latest Instruction) | Recommended Disposition
----------------------------------|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------
Indemnification basket structure  | Deductible basket                      | Converted to tipping basket           | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities   | Concede basket conversion           | ACCEPT / CONCEDE (document expressly; condition on Schedule 5.2 exclusions)
Indemnification cap               | Stated Debtor Plan cap                 | Silently reduced                      | Schedule 5.2; valuation summary     | Not conceded                        | REJECT; restore cap; require conspicuous redline and disclosure/valuation update
MAE — regulatory-action carve-outs| No carve-out for at-issue regulatory action | Carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue | Schedule 3.7 (two pending inquiries)| Not conceded                        | REJECT; fallback only as narrowly limited to disclosed existence without adverse developments
Survival / limitation period      | Exhibit B survival matrix              | New shorter limitation period for core reps | Exhibit B (controls)                | WALK-AWAY if reduced                | REJECT — walk-away; reaffirm Exhibit B as exclusive survival schedule

Rule of construction applied throughout: scheduled exceptions and Exhibit B control over general statements in the base bankruptcy-restructuring materials and over conflicting general language in the Committee Markup.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
V. INTERACTIONS AMONG DEVIATIONS (COMPOUNDING RISK)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The three deviations are not independent. Accepted together, they would:

  1. Shrink the economic backstop (lower silent cap + tipping basket drawing on a smaller pool), while
  2. Removing MAE leverage over the precise regulatory risks disclosed on Schedule 3.7, while
  3. Shortening the temporal window (contra Exhibit B) in which core-rep breaches — including regulatory and retained-liability related breaches — may be asserted.

Even with the client-directed concession on basket structure alone, accepting either the cap reduction or the MAE carve-outs alongside any survival cut would reallocate risk in ways not supported by the valuation summary or the disclosure-statement excerpts. The walk-away on survival therefore also functions as a circuit-breaker against the full compounding package.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VI. DISCLOSURE-STATEMENT AND VALUATION CONFORMING ITEMS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Before any revised plan is filed or re-solicited, the following conforming workstreams are required for any accepted change (and should be previewed in committee negotiations as debtor requirements):

  • Update disclosure-statement indemnity economics to reflect tipping-basket mechanics and any final cap figure; expressly describe Schedule 5.2's interaction with basket and cap.
  • Refresh valuation summary sensitivity for indemnity drag and retained-liability scenarios under the final basket/cap construct.
  • Align MAE risk-factor language with the final MAE definition; Schedule 3.7 inquiries must remain accurately described relative to plan conditions and termination/MAE rights.
  • Confirm Exhibit B survival matrix is reproduced or expressly incorporated; delete or conform any narrative limitation-period language in the disclosure statement that would suggest a shorter core-rep survival than Exhibit B.
  • Transmittal package to the committee should attach a blackline of plan indemnification, MAE, and survival provisions, plus a one-page schedule mapping Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B to the final language, so no "silent" change can recur.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VII. RECOMMENDED NEXT-STEP MARKUP POSTURE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  1. ACCEPT the tipping-basket conversion only, expressly and in isolation, conditioned on full Schedule 5.2 exclusion from basket tipping and cap burn.
  2. REJECT the silent indemnification-cap reduction; restore Debtor Plan cap; demand conspicuous numeric blackline in any future proposal.
  3. REJECT MAE regulatory-action carve-outs keyed to the at-issue conduct; offer only the narrow fallback in Section III.Deviation 2.E.3 if commercially necessary.
  4. REJECT any shortening of core-representation survival; reaffirm Exhibit B as exclusive; treat further pressure on this point as a walk-away under the controlling partner instruction.
  5. Require simultaneous conforming edits to disclosure-statement excerpts and valuation summary before circulating a revised Debtor Plan or joint plan.
  6. Preserve on the record that earlier deal-team messages with contrary priority ordering are superseded by the latest controlling instruction reflected in this report.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VIII. CONCLUSION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Reconciled against the Debtor Plan, the Committee Markup, Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B, the valuation and disclosure excerpts those schedules embody, and the controlling deal-team correspondence, only one deviation is within the client's authorized concession (basket conversion to a tipping basket). The silent indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs should be rejected or, at most, tightly limited with full schedule and disclosure conformity. The shortened survival / limitation period for core representations contradicts Exhibit B and is a walk-away issue; it must be rejected in full.

This deviation report is the operative deliverable for the engagement instruction: compare the committee's redlined plan against the debtor's original plan, using the valuation summary, transmittal context, and disclosure-statement excerpts, and address every deviation.

Respectfully submitted,
Restructuring Deal Team
